title: Lean Axiom Bundle / Attack Surface v0

canonical_node.axiom: All load-bearing assumptions must be collected into a single visible, attackable bundle; downstream proofs must trace to that bundle; bridge claims and theological identifications must be explicitly labeled and separated from formal theorems.
definitions: Assumption Bundle: a small, explicit, named set of primitive assumptions that Lean is allowed to assume.
Bridge claim: a statement that maps a formal result to a theological or empirical concept, not proven by Lean.
Theological identification: a claim that a formal object corresponds to a specific theological entity (e.g., Christ).
Anti-smuggling rule: no theorem may import a theological conclusion as an unnoticed premise.
Public claim labels: CANON, LEAN_SUPPORTED, RUNTIME_SUPPORTED, STRONG_BUT_NEEDS_SOURCING, USEFUL_BUT_UNVERIFIED, SPECULATIVE, OPEN_BRIDGE, CONTRADICTED, QUARANTINE.
derivation: Scattered assumptions across files make auditing difficult and allow smuggling.
Therefore, collect all load-bearing assumptions into one visible bundle.
Separate primitive assumptions, definitions, bridge assumptions, theological identifications, empirical assumptions, and open conjectures.
Theorems should run downstream from the bundle and definitions.
Bridge claims and theological identifications must be labeled and not presented as Lean proofs.
Critics should be directed to attack the bundle, definitions, inference steps, bridge assumptions, theological identifications, empirical evidence, or public wording overclaims.
canonical_node.action: Implement a formal project structure with a single AxiomBundle file, definitions file, theorem files that accept the bundle as a parameter, and metadata files for bridge claims and public claim status. Ensure every theorem traces back to the bundle and every bridge claim is labeled.
boundary: Does not claim that Lean proves God or any theological conclusion.
Does not define the final theology; the minimum bundle is a first attackable core.
Does not allow theorems to silently import theological premises.
Does not treat definitions as discoveries; they are controlled vocabulary.
test: Check that all load-bearing assumptions are listed in the AxiomBundle file.
Check that no theorem file invents fresh assumptions outside the bundle.
Check that bridge claims and theological identifications are labeled as such.
Check that public claims carry one of the defined support labels.
Check that the anti-smuggling rule is enforced: no theorem imports a theological conclusion as an unnoticed premise.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured method to make all assumptions explicit and attackable, enabling honest auditing and preventing smuggling of conclusions.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to prove conditional structural theorems under stated assumptions, as already demonstrated by the Prover9 toy theorem.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this bundle, the formal system becomes scattered and un-auditable, allowing critics to fairly claim smuggling and undermining the credibility of downstream results.
dg5_translation_registers: Public claim status -> Excel field assumption_bundle_dependency

overstatement_risks: May be interpreted as claiming that the bundle itself is proven or that the listed assumptions are true.
May be interpreted as claiming that the formal system can prove theological conclusions if the bundle is accepted.
May be interpreted as claiming that the minimum bundle is sufficient for all downstream results.
kill_conditions: If the bundle is not actually used consistently in all downstream proofs.
If bridge claims are presented as formal theorems without proper labeling.
If the anti-smuggling rule is violated.
risk.lean_target: Implement the AxiomBundle structure and a few downstream theorems that accept the bundle as a parameter, demonstrating the pattern.

plain_summary: This document defines a methodological standard for organizing Lean formalizations of Theophysics: collect all assumptions into a single visible bundle, separate definitions and bridge claims, and ensure every theorem traces back to the bundle. It does not prove any theological claim but provides a structure for honest formal reasoning.
